items.title: Activation of Amino Acids and the Phases of Translation

source_refs.note: Activation of amino acids and the three phases of translation (PDF 137-140), as printed; Figures 19.17 to 19.20 are replaced by original diagrams.

blocks.text: Before protein synthesis, the assemblage units are prepared. Specific tRNAs attach with specific amino acids and make aminoacyl-tRNAs (aa-tRNA). The enzyme aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase carries out this reaction. There are 20 kinds of this enzyme. Each kind binds to a specific amino acid. It also recognizes and binds to the tRNA with anticodons for that amino acid. The aa-tRNA delivers the amino acid to the ribosome for incorporation into the polypeptide chain.

blocks.alt: Left: a large green enzyme, aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase, holding an amino acid in one pocket and a tRNA in another, with the tRNA's anticodon end inside the enzyme. An arrow leads to the released aminoacyl-tRNA, the amino acid joined to the top of the tRNA, ready to participate in protein synthesis.
blocks.caption: Figure 19.17: Activation of amino acids (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 19.17).
